correctness.rationale: All SU(2) normalization and mixed moments follow from orthonormal characters, the exact tensor-product identity and a triangle-count closed form for every integer n>=0. The sixth moment of complex pairs is derived with central parity, not by assuming real coefficients. Explicit endpoint derivative signs and positive leading coefficient of the derivative quadratic prove a unique interior maximum. Exact cubic factorization and strict derivative sign prove the global deficit and sharp modulus constant. Independent integer tensor-product computations for n=0..30, high-order Chebyshev quadrature at 124 complex test configurations, and 1581 grid deficit tests agree; only the analytic argument proves all n.

value.rationale: The natural adjacent spectral two-mode subspace of normalized zonal spherical harmonics on S^3 (equivalently consecutive SU(2) characters) is a basic testing ground for concentration and reverse-Holder/Nikolskii inequalities. The theorem determines its exact sixth-moment amplification at every degree, shows forced real relative phase and a nontrivial degree-dependent imbalance, gives the high-frequency growth, and supplies an exact globally positive stability functional. Those exact quantities are not supplied by the cited general growth estimates and can be used as sharp two-mode benchmarks; this is more than a raw tensor-product table or a single-index calculation.
